[WP] "I woke up with blood on my hands and smiled."
I woke up with blood on my hands and smiled. Not pregnant.

They don't tell you the face of evil will be smiling. Those grinning soldiers would joke and chat by the water cooler while we sat in cages 50 yards away. Their eyes would pass over us - our suffering was a particularly dull background to their mundane lives. The darkest part of our nature might be our lack of empathy for those we have deemed "other".

Certainly, as a prisoner of war I was treated well. By the standards of history, modern prisoners are practically pampered pets. We're fed. We're not tortured. We even have a pretty good chance of returning home after the war. But boredom inspires creativity in prison guards. The bounds of the Geneva Convention were, after all, less solid than my own.

Isolation is a unique sort of abuse. Bland food. No communication. No light. Nothing to do. After a few weeks, you start to dig into the recedes of your mind for anything new to think about...

I'd fantasize about what I'd do if I ever got out. I'd toy with the idea of finding a girl and getting married. I had a list of foods memorized, in order, that I was going to eat. But the dark places my mind would circle around to - the revenge I'd get on the guards - that was perhaps the most vivid dreamscape I would visit.

And then the day finally came. My home country had won the war, and as part of the treaty the prisons were ordered to release all prisoners of war. And I had my opportunity, at last, to satisfy those months of fantasy. How could I justify any other action?

I remember those first few kills most fondly. The crunch of the first man's skull against the stone wall. The thunder of the gun as I marched towards the main office. You know, I don't even know if the man I found there was someone important. He was certainly someone important to me. I locked the door and held him at the other side of the room with the gun. I had envisioned so many ways of rectifying my imprisonment, I knew it would be hours before I was through with him.

I woke up with blood on my hands and smiled. The airplane would be landing shortly and I would be back in my home country. I knew the passengers around me were probably looking at my orange jump suit and manacles and assuming that I was an evil man. Perhaps they were right. I had killed and torture - they had only left me alone.
